title: Liberty Leading the People
official_description: Delacroix combines a real Parisian barricade with an allegorical woman personifying Liberty during the July Revolution of 1830.
historical_context: The painting responds to the Three Glorious Days of 27-29 July 1830, when Parisians rose against King Charles X.
visual_description: Liberty strides over a barricade holding the French tricolour and a rifle while an armed crowd advances through smoke and fallen bodies.

chunks.text: Eugene Delacroix painted Liberty Leading the People in 1830. Its complete title refers to 28 July 1830.
The scene does not show the French Revolution of 1789. It refers to the July Revolution of 27, 28, and 29 July 1830.
During those three days, Parisians built barricades and rose against King Charles X, defending freedoms that included freedom of the press.
The central woman is both an ideal classical figure and a woman of the people. She personifies the abstract idea of Liberty.
Liberty moves forward over a barricade, raising the French tricolour in one hand and carrying a rifle in the other.
She wears a Phrygian cap, a historical emblem of freedom, and her yellow garment recalls drapery from classical antiquity.
Delacroix repeats blue, white, and red across the composition, visually echoing the tricolour flag that Liberty holds above the crowd.
The advancing figures form a strong pyramid, with Liberty and the flag at the peak, making the movement feel forceful and upward.
The monumental oil painting measures 2.6 metres high by 3.25 metres wide and carries the Louvre inventory number RF 129.
Delacroix painted it in Paris from September to December 1830, only months after the uprising, and signed and dated it in red paint.
The painting was shown at the Salon of 1831, purchased from Delacroix by the French state that August, and moved to the Louvre in 1874.
The image became an internationally reused symbol of liberty and freedom struggles, even though it began with one specific Parisian uprising.
Delacroix painted people crossing a barricade in Paris. A brave figure called Liberty holds the French flag high and leads everyone forward.
The official record traces an unstable display history after the 1831 state purchase: periods at the Luxembourg, storage, return during 1848, and final transfer to the Louvre in November 1874.
Eugene Delacroix a peint La Liberte guidant le peuple en 1830. Le titre complet renvoie au 28 juillet 1830.
Le tableau ne montre pas la Revolution francaise de 1789. Il represente les Trois Glorieuses des 27, 28 et 29 juillet 1830.
Les Parisiens ont dresse des barricades contre le roi Charles X pour defendre leurs libertes, notamment celle de la presse.
La femme centrale est a la fois une deesse classique et une femme du peuple. Elle personnifie l'idee de Liberte.
La Liberte franchit une barricade, leve le drapeau tricolore et porte un fusil. Un bonnet phrygien couvre sa tete.
Les personnages forment une pyramide puissante dont la Liberte et le drapeau occupent le sommet.
Expose au Salon de 1831, le tableau a ete achete par l'Etat francais la meme annee et a rejoint le Louvre en 1874.
